item.text: {"question_id":"4B.8","answer":"Tshisekedi sought and received party endorsement for a second five-year term and personally stated that the Constitution permitted his candidacy; the supplied constitutional text does not independently verify that basis. [BATCH-0005-E008, BATCH-0018-E006] The Constitutional Court validated 26 presidential candidacies, rejected challenges to Tshisekedi and Katumbi, and reinstated two candidates previously excluded by CENI, providing limited procedural safeguards, although the evidence does not establish judicial or presidential independence. [BATCH-0005-E005] The presidential and legislative elections occurred on the normal legal schedule, but Tshisekedi was re-elected and his Sacred Union coalition and allies won 450 of 477 confirmed legislative seats, leaving no opposition transfer test and potentially reducing institutional constraint; the evidence does not show that he personally engineered this result. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0028-E011] The process was materially qualified by delayed and extended voting, nonvoting in conflict-affected areas, annulled constituencies, disputed tabulation, documented anomalies, and allegations that CENI and the Constitutional Court were politicized. [BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0028-E018] The coordinator’s appeal for rivals to accept the result and prepare for 2028 was not a personal acceptance by Tshisekedi of an adverse result. [BATCH-0006-E006] The Court’s confirmation and authorization to swear in occurred in January 2024 and are retrospective adjudication or legal formalities concerning the 2023 election, not evidence that 2023 transfer safeguards were independent or fully credible. [BATCH-0007-E001, BATCH-0018-E009, BATCH-0015-E001] Overall, the evidence supports formal electoral continuity, candidate validation, and an asserted constitutional second-term basis, but it does not robustly establish compliance with independently constraining succession rules or demonstrate willingness to accept a lawful transfer of
